title: Perfectness is checked on stalks or on residue field fibres, and for bounded below complexes all the conditions agree

standard_prerequisites.name: Perfectness is preserved by pulling back along a flat localization and along the residue field maps, so the implications among the first five conditions follow from those pullbacks
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the implications from the first condition down to the fibre conditions, and the equivalence of the prime and maximal ideal forms.

standard_prerequisites.name: A pseudo-coherent complex over a local ring whose fibre has vanishing cohomology below a degree splits as the direct sum of a perfect upper truncation and a lower truncation, leaving the lower part to be killed
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the local implication to showing that the lower truncation vanishes.

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite module whose reduction modulo the maximal ideal is nonzero is nonzero by Nakayama's lemma, and a bounded below pseudo-coherent complex can be made perfect after a localization
standard_prerequisites.use: Kills the lower truncation in the local case and finishes the bounded below case by choosing a localization at an element outside any given maximal ideal.

core_obligations: Derive the implications among the first five conditions: perfectness pulls back along localizations, primes are contained in maximal ideals so the maximal ideal condition implies the prime one, and the residue field conditions follow by pulling back along the residue maps (proof lines 20088-20096).

Reduce the equivalence with the fibre conditions to the local case: assume the ring is local and that the fibre has vanishing cohomology below some degree a, and announce that perfectness will follow (proof lines 20098-20102).

Apply the splitting statement to the complex to write it as the direct sum of its two truncations with the upper one perfect and of tor amplitude starting at a, so that only the vanishing of the lower truncation remains to be shown (proof lines 20102-20106).

Show the lower truncation vanishes: if not, take the largest degree in which its cohomology M is nonzero, note that M is finite because the truncation is pseudo-coherent, use Nakayama to conclude that its reduction modulo the maximal ideal is nonzero, and obtain a contradiction with the vanishing assumption on the fibre (proof lines 20106-20120).

Settle the bounded below case: assuming the equivalent conditions and boundedness below, pick a maximal ideal and use the lifting statement together with the glueing statement for perfectness and quasi-compactness of the spectrum to find an element outside that maximal ideal after which the complex becomes perfect, which gives condition (1) (proof lines 20122-20132).
proof_roadmap: Get the chain of implications from pullback invariance of perfectness (proof lines 20088-20096).
In the local case, split off the perfect upper truncation and kill the lower one by a Nakayama argument on its top cohomology (proof lines 20098-20120).
In the bounded below case, localize at an element outside a chosen maximal ideal to obtain perfectness globally (proof lines 20122-20132).
difficulty_reason: The statement collects five conditions on a pseudo-coherent complex, namely perfectness, perfectness of all localizations at primes, at maximal ideals, and the vanishing of the fibre cohomology below all degrees at primes and at maximal ideals, and shows a chain of implications that becomes a full equivalence for bounded below complexes (statement lines 20063-20086). The proof first derives the easy implications from the invariance of perfectness under pullback, then treats the hard local implication by cutting the complex into its two truncations, one of which is perfect with tor amplitude starting at the given degree, after which the lower truncation is shown to vanish by a Nakayama argument on its top cohomology module (proof lines 20088-20120). The bounded below case is closed by localizing at an element outside an arbitrary maximal ideal using the lifting and glueing statements.
